    NFSv3: use nfs_add_or_obtain() to create and reference inodes
    
    Signed-off-by: Benjamin Coddington <bcodding@redhat.com>
    Signed-off-by: Anna Schumaker <Anna.Schumaker@Netapp.com>

diff --git a/fs/nfs/nfs3proc.c b/fs/nfs/nfs3proc.c
index a3ad2d46fd42..9eb2f1a503ab 100644
--- a/fs/nfs/nfs3proc.c
+++ b/fs/nfs/nfs3proc.c
@@ -279,15 +279,17 @@ static
bic_trace_step.reason: In nfs3_proc_create, after calling nfs3_do_create (which returns d_alias via nfs_add_or_obtain), the code unconditionally replaces dentry with d_alias if it is non-NULL (line: 'if (d_alias) dentry = d_alias;'). There is no check to verify that the returned alias is not a directory. This means if d_splice_alias returns a directory dentry, the subsequent operations (such as nfs_post_op_update_inode and nfs3_proc_setacls on d_inode(dentry)) will treat a directory inode as a file, leading to an oops. The commit does not add any such check, so the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is absent.
